Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 103, verses 1–3:

(p-509) Surat al-ʿAsr is Meccan and it has three verses.

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿By time,﴾ ﴿indeed, mankind is in loss,﴾ ﴿except for those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience.﴾

This surah is Meccan according to Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn al-Zubayr and the majority, and Medinan according to Mujahid, Qatadah and Muqatil. When it had said, regarding what precedes it, ﴿Rivalry in worldly gain distracts you﴾ [al-Takathur 102:1], and the threat was made by repeating ﴿Nay, you are going to know﴾ [al-Takathur 102:3], it clarified the condition of the believer and the disbeliever.

﴿By time (al-ʿasr)﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the age (al-dahr). It is said of it ʿaṣr, ʿiṣr and ʿuṣr. God swore by it because of the varieties of wonders in its passing. Qatadah said: al-ʿasr is the afternoon (al-ʿashiyy), He swore by it as He swore by the forenoon (al-ḍuha), because of the signs of power in both of them. It was also said: al-ʿasr is the day and the night, and from this is the statement of Humayd ibn Thawr:

*And the two ʿasrs will not delay a day and a night, when they seek to overtake what they have aimed at.*

It was also said: al-ʿasr is the early part of the day (bukra) and al-ʿasr is the late part of the day (ʿashiyya), and these are the two cooler times (al-abradan). According to this view and the one before it, the oath is sworn by one of them without specification. Muqatil said: al-ʿasr is the middle prayer (al-ṣalah al-wusta), by which He swore. Al-Zamakhshari began with this view and said: because of its excellence, by the evidence of His saying ﴿and the middle prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:238], the prayer of ʿasr, in the codex of Hafsa, and His saying: "Whoever misses the prayer of ʿasr, it is as if his family and property were taken from him," because the difficulty in performing it is greater, due to people's bustle in their trade and their reckoning at the end of the day and their occupation with their livelihoods. End of quote. Salam recited ﴿al-ʿasr﴾ with a kasra on the ṣad, and (al-ṣabr) with a kasra on the ba. Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: this is not permitted except in pause, by transferring the vowel (naql al-ḥarakah). It is narrated from Abu ʿAmr: (bi-l-ṣabr) with a kasra on the ba in the mode of ishmam, and this too is only in pause. End of quote. In al-Kamil of al-Hudhali: (al-ʿiṣr, al-ṣiṭr, al-fijr, al-witr), with a kasra on what precedes the sakin in all of these, are Harun and Ibn Musa from Abu ʿAmr, and the rest read with sukun as the community does. End of quote. Ibn Khalawayh said: ﴿wa-tawaṣaw bi-l-ṣabr﴾ with transfer of the vowel from Abu ʿAmr. Sahib al-Lawamih, ʿIsa of Basra, said: (bi-l-ṣabir), transferring the vowel of the ra to the ba, so that one does not need to bring part of the vowel in pause, nor to make it sukun and join two sakins together. This is a widespread dialect, not anomalous but well-attested, and it indicates the case-ending and separation from the meeting of two sakins, and its basis is that the pausal form should be sukun. End of quote. We have cited in explanation of this, in the Sharh al-Tashil, several verses, such as the saying of the rajiz:

*I am Jarir, my kunya is Abu ʿAmir, I strike with the sword, and Saʿd is in the ʿaṣir.*

He means Abu ʿAmr. And al-ʿasr. And al-insan is a collective noun that covers all, and for this reason the exception from it is valid. And al-khusr is al-khusran, like al-kufr and al-kufran. And what loss is greater than that of one who loses this world and the Hereafter?

Ibn Hurmuz, Zayd ibn ʿAli, and Harun from Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read ﴿khusur﴾ with a damma on the sin, while the majority read it with sukun. Whoever sells his Hereafter for his worldly life is in the utmost loss, unlike the believer, for he has bought the Hereafter with this world, so he profits and is made happy.

﴿And enjoin one another to truth﴾: that is, to the established command from those who act upon it and enjoin one another to it. ﴿And enjoin one another to patience﴾: in obedience to God the Exalted, and in abstaining from sins.
